parole.testo: From hibbeln + -ig. The verb is a Rhine Franconian or East Central German form of hüpfeln, frequentative of hüpfen (“to hop”).

From Middle High German hünkel, from older huoniclīn, from Old High German huoninklīn, diminutive of huon, whence modern Huhn (“chicken”). The unrounded vowel -i- follows Rhine Franconian dialects, in which the word is chiefly used. Cognate with Luxembourgish Hénkel.

Originally a Rhine Franconian dialect word denoting a number of menhirs in Hesse. Generalised and standardised in the 19th century. The form is analysable as Hinkel (“chicken”) + Stein (“stone”). parole.significato: dormer; dormer-window (roofed projection from a sloping roof with a window at the front)
parole.testo: From late Middle High German gūpe. Further origin unknown. Since the word is apparently from Rhine Franconian dialects, identity with Kuppe (“top, knoll”), itself also a Central German form, is possible. The long vowel is problematic, however, though it might be due to conflation with a related word
